recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-47281 unless the work group later changes the architectural scope of out-of-band subscription notification services.
issue_request: FHIR-47281 was an Applied FHIR-core R6 subscriptions issue with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The reporter said the Subscriptions Framework definition of Server as a FHIR application was vague and suggested FHIR server wording unless notification-only out-of-band systems were intentionally supported. The accepted resolution clarified that subscription functionality can be provided by a FHIR Server or by another application such as a monitoring system converting internal events into FHIR notifications, without implying REST API exposure.
initial_application: Commit 48703074e9d25cda8fb6304808769fe4a10a3b1a, titled FHIR-47281 - subscription server actor clarification, already changed source/subscriptions.html to add the approved Server actor examples and an adjacent note about architectures that separate subscription notification services from a FHIR Server. The Jira comment links this application to HL7/fhir#3967, which was merged on 2025-11-09.
additional_context: source/subscriptions.html is in current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml, which lists subscriptions.html as the Subscriptions page under the Exchange module. FHIR-I minutes for 2025-03-31 include FHIR-47281 in the R6 Subscriptions block vote and record the motion to approve the block vote 17-0-0. Zulip evidence found only the corresponding block-vote announcement and no conflicting substantive discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already says Server refers to the FHIR application or applications acting as the subscription provider, such as a FHIR Server or monitoring system converting internal events into FHIR notifications, and the note already clarifies that subscription implementations are not required to expose a FHIR REST API themselves.
